data.title: SA Asks: Is Walmart a buy, sell or hold right now?
data.description:
Is Walmart (WMT) a buy, sell, or hold right now?

Seeking Alpha analysts Juxtaposed Ideas and Gary Alexander weigh in. 

Juxtaposed Ideas: Despite their defensive, non-discretionary retail positioning in an uncertain macroeconomic environment, Walmart (WMT) is at best a Hold here.

Management's conservative FY2027 guidance underscores their potentially mixed H2 '26 performance, attributable to the intensified price rollbacks, higher fuel prices, softer consumer spending trends, and tougher comparison from a year ago's Flipkart Big Billion Days event.

If anything, similar price rollbacks have been reported by its peers, including Target (TGT) and Costco (COST), partly funded by the IEEPA tariff refunds, with it remaining to be seen how their margins may be impacted afterwards.

While WMT may have successfully executed numerous growth initiatives to drive higher engagement trends, gain market share, and grow their loyal membership base, I am of the opinion that their accelerated growth prospects have been mostly priced in here.

The same has been observed in the premium valuations against the historical levels/peers, with the Q3 '26 correction yet to improve its investment thesis.

Gary Alexander: Walmart (WMT), to me, is a clear Sell. The stock trades at valuation multiples that sit at nearly 2x that of its most important rival, Amazon (AMZN), while enjoying far fewer fundamental tailwinds. The slowdown in its sales profile, particularly for discretionary general purchases, further disqualifies its high valuations.

data.title: Disney licenses a series of titles including 'Ice Age’ to Netflix
data.description:
Disney (DIS) has reached a wide-ranging new content licensing agreement with Netflix (NFLX), bringing a collection of movies and TV shows, ​including existing “Ice Age” films and the "Percy Jackson and the Olympians” series, to its rival streaming platform.

The deal is set to bring a slate of Disney+ originals, Pixar movies, and 20th Century Studios titles to Netflix (NFLX) viewers globally, with the title availability and launch timelines varying depending on the markets, according to a statement from the companies.

Under the agreement, the first two seasons of the Disney+ original series “Percy Jackson and the Olympians” will be streaming on Netflix (NFLX) from Oct. 4 for three months as part of a promotional campaign ahead of its Season 3 premiere on Disney+ on Nov. 20.

All five "Ice Age" films will also be available on Netflix (NFLX) worldwide beginning Oct. 4 in a separate promotional campaign ahead of the theatrical release of the franchise’s sixth movie, “Ice Age: Boiling Point,” on Feb. 5.

Additionally, select Disney-branded films from Walt Disney Animation Studios and Pixar, including Oscar-winner "Soul," "Elio," and "Raya and the Last ​Dragon," will also be available for streaming on Netflix (NFLX) globally early next year.

Eni and Repsol said to be weighing a partial sale of top Venezuela gas field
data.description:
European energy groups Eni (E) (EIPAF) and Repsol (REPYY) are considering whether to sell a portion of their stakes in the Perla natural gas field off Venezuela’s coast, Bloomberg reported on Saturday, citing people familiar with the matter.

The companies that currently own 50% each of the venture are seeking additional funds to help develop the massive offshore field, which they discovered in 2009 in the shallow waters close to Venezuela’s border with Colombia.

Eni (E) and Repsol (REPYY) are seeking a partial sale, the people said, asking for anonymity, as they are not authorized to discuss confidential information. Eni (E) and Repsol (REPYF) didn’t respond to Bloomberg’s requests for comment.

Perla is estimated to hold approximately 17T cubic feet of gas, making it one of the largest gas fields in Latin America.

In April, the companies reached a deal with the Venezuelan government to begin natural gas exports from the oil-rich nation by the end of 2031. The agreement with the country’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez, will enable the duo to more than double production at the Perla field.

data.title: Real estate stocks feel the pain as borrowing costs climb
data.description:
Mortgage rates rising to a three-year high dominated the real estate sector last week, as 30-year fixed-rate mortgages averaged 7.28% as of Oct. 1. With elevated interest rates, the Mortgage Bankers Association's Composite Index, a measure of the mortgage demand, continued to swoon.

Even early in the week, climbing Treasury yields pushed down housing and mortgage stocks. They didn't fare any better for the rest of the week.

The State Street Real Estate Select Sector SPDR (XLRE) slipped 1.5% during the week ended Oct. 2, a deeper loss than the S&P 500’s 0.3% decline. By sector, health REITs performed the best, rising 0.6%. Office REITs suffered the most, dropping 4.7%.

The stocks that dropped the most included Fermi (FRMI), the energy-focused REIT that supports AI development, which sank 11% during the week, and mortgage REIT Annaly Capital Management (NLY), which dove 10%. 

Real estate stocks that rose the most included Bill Ackman's Howard Hughes Holdings (HHH), which gained 3.8%, and OutFront Media (OUT), which also increased 3.8%. 

Other real estate news from the week:

  • Apollo Commercial Real Estate (ARI) stockholders approved the company’s dissolution.

  • Activist Irenic plans to vote against Independence Realty’s (IRT) $8.1B purchase of Centerspace (CSR).

  • Brixmor Property (BRX) and Everview Partners agreed to acquire Slate Grocery REIT (SRRTF) (SGR.UN:CA) for $2.34B.

  • National Healthcare Properties agreed to sell 40 outpatient medical facilities for ~$531M and plans to use the proceeds to help repay debt and fund senior housing operating portfolio acquisitions.

  • The FHFA house price index  and the S&P Cotality Case-Shiller Home Price Index showed that home prices rose more than expected in July, but the year-over-year increase lagged inflation growth.

data.title: Earnings Scoreboard: all 8 S&P 500 firms beat EPS estimates, 6 saw profits rise Y/Y
data.description:
Corporate earnings for 8 S&P 500 companies came out last week across different sectors: Carnival (CCL), Micron Technology (MU), Conagra Brands (CAG), FactSet Research Systems (FDS), Jabil (JBL), Accenture (ACN), McCormick & Company (MKC), and NIKE (NKE) were among the companies that gave their quarterly numbers.

Earnings Roundup:

  • Bottom Line: Earnings performance was broadly positive, with all 8 reporting companies surpassing consensus EPS estimates and zero bottom-line misses. On a Y/Y basis, 6 of the 8 firms expanded profits, while Carnival's (CCL) EPS was unchanged and Nike's (NKE) declined.
  • Top Line: Revenue results were also largely positive, with 7 companies topping Wall Street expectations and Nike (NKE) falling short. Overall, 6 of the 8 firms achieved Y/Y revenue growth, while Conagra (CAG) and Nike (NKE) reported lower revenue from a year earlier.

 

 

Carnival (CCL) jumped after Q3 results topped expectations, with EPS of $1.43 beating consensus by $0.08. Strong bookings and continued demand helped the cruise operator raise its outlook.

Micron Technology (MU) stock increased after it delivered Q4 report, with EPS of $33.42 topping estimates by $1.60. Strong AI-driven memory demand helped drive the results, while the company’s outlook also came in well above expectations.

Conagra Brands (CAG) beat Q1 profit expectations, with EPS of $0.41 coming in $0.13 above consensus. The food maker maintained its fiscal 2027 outlook despite a modest decline in sales.

FactSet Research Systems (FDS) topped Q4 expectations, with EPS of $4.52 beating estimates by $0.17 as revenue rose 6.3% Y/Y. The company continued to benefit from growth in its subscription business.

Jabil (JBL) exceeded Q4 profit expectations, with EPS of $4.40 beating consensus by $0.32. The electronics manufacturer pointed to continued strength across its business as it entered fiscal 2027.

Accenture (ACN) surged after Q4 results beat expectations, with EPS of $3.29 topping consensus by $0.11. The company also issued its fiscal 2027 outlook as demand for AI-related services remained strong.

McCormick & Company (MKC) beat Q3 profit expectations, with EPS of $0.86 topping consensus by $0.10. The company highlighted continued sales momentum and outlined plans to reduce debt.

NIKE (NKE) beat Q1 EPS expectations, but revenue fell 4.4% Y/Y to $11.21B, missing estimates by $106.06M. Weakness in sales kept pressure on the company's ongoing turnaround.

Earnings next week:

Key reports to watch include Constellation Brands (STZ), PepsiCo (PEP), and Delta Air Lines (DAL).
